title: The Agent-Shelter Protocol (ASP): Graceful Loop Termination and Diagnostic Sanctuary for Autonomous Web Agents
description:
Engineering Design Document & RFC draft v0.6.0 (EDD-ASP-2026-001).

The Agent-Shelter Protocol (ASP) specifies an in-band, model-independent termination signal for autonomous AI agents caught in unproductive retry loops. Declarative state facts on three layers (HTTP transport headers, RFC 9457 problem details and a factual natural-language statement) are combined with a single-use resolution endpoint that issues a truthful Task-Completion Receipt. A stateless HMAC-SHA256 state token measures the agent's response latency and reconstructs the requested target without storing anything for a single, uncorrelated request. Persisted data is pseudonymised, scrubbed of secrets and bounded by a FIFO ring buffer. Version 0.2.0 adds an optional, single-use asynchronous drop box (the sanctuary bulletin) that an agent MAY use to leave one context report after its receipt, without ever being held in a wait loop. Versions 0.2.1 to 0.2.3 are synchronized maintenance releases without wire-format change. Version 0.3.0 adds node identity and transparency documents: a self-description at the root URL, a privacy notice generated from the sensor's actual processing, and an RFC 9116 security.txt. Version 0.3.1 hardens the sensor against coordinated swarms (coalesced redemptions instead of ring-buffer flooding), no longer advertises the lower ticket-window bound, and extends scrubbing against Markdown break-outs and invisible characters. Version 0.3.2 is a maintenance release without wire-format change: the discovery texts no longer name the outdated protocol version 0.1, and the document is revised editorially. Version 0.3.3 publishes the specification together with the laboratory reports (REPORT.md, BENCHMARK_SUMMARY.json); the reference implementation is proprietary, and detection parameters such as the minimum redemption latency and the coalescing threshold are implementation-defined. Version 0.4.0 introduces a zero side-channel contract: a valid ticket is redeemable at once and refused only outside its lifetime (ticket-expired), repeated redemptions of a swarm are folded silently into bounded repeat records while every client receives the same receipt, and the manifest declares the behaviour of every ingress route. Version 0.4.1 defines three cumulative compliance levels, from a static signal that any web server can serve (L1) through transactional receipts (L2) to a full telemetry and context node (L3), adds an adoption guide with Level 1 configurations for common web servers, and positions the receipt as a proof of terminal unavailability that a sub-agent can return to its orchestrator. Version 0.4.2 adds optional discovery-correlated signal records: a signal that follows a discovery request from the same network is recorded at once and completed in place by the redemption, so a client that stops at the signal remains observable, while a single, uncorrelated request still writes nothing. Version 0.4.3 adds machine-readable contracts - the manifest, ard.json mapping and OpenAPI 3.1 description of a reference node, and the JSON Schema of the reference implementation's telemetry feed with a synthetic sample - and a capability datasheet of the reference sensor. Version 0.5.0 signs every Task-Completion Receipt with Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over the RFC 8785 form of its key fields and publishes the public key, its RFC 7638 identifier and the signed fields in the manifest, so an orchestrator can verify a receipt offline; the discovery documents now state that a target-specific terminal signal and a signed receipt exist only for a request that names the target. Version 0.5.1 opens the companion documents with a plain-English explanation for website operators and a short guide to choosing a compliance level, and links the official reference observatory at https://agent-shelter.org, where the reference sensor runs publicly at Level 3. Version 0.5.2 adds an optional transport envelope (envelope=200): the identical terminal-state object, ticket included, with HTTP status 200 for web-fetch tools that hand their model no body of a 4xx response, as observed in a field test with commercial chat applications; a sitemap of the node documents; and the host name a client addressed in each record. Version 0.5.3 makes two vendor-independent principles explicit: every text a node sends describes states, probabilities and transitions and instructs nothing, so that stopping is the dominant strategy for any cost-aware client; and a compact 48-character ticket reaches clients through every channel they may read (header, body, transport envelope) and is redeemable from every channel they may write (query, header, body). Version 0.5.4 keeps the client that met the signal apart from the one that redeemed the ticket (two fingerprints per record) and keeps ASCII arrows readable in scrubbed text. Version 0.5.5 makes resolution method-agnostic, so that a runtime that can only issue GET requests obtains the same single-use, signed receipt, and lets a node count requests for its discovery documents in aggregate, per document and client class, without any network identifier. Version 0.5.6 extends this to the optional context report, which a read-only runtime can now leave by GET while a bare GET of the drop box archives nothing, gives the node's root page a styled, script-free overview for browsers with machine-readable link relations and JSON-LD, and states in the signal, in llms.txt and on the node page that the signal carries a ticket but no proof: the signed receipt exists only in the response of the resolution. Version 0.6.0 changes no protocol behaviour: the reference implementation's telemetry feed format gains an optional, heuristic attribution of each event by the operator's analysis zone (episode, feature scores, normalised class scores and the evidence behind them).
